# GripPoint

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/interaction/physics-hold/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/GripPoint.cs#L80)

A place on a grabbable where a hand may attach, who may attach there, and what the hand does once
it has - including the shape it takes, when that has been authored.

This is the whole of "this object has a right way to be held". A Grabbable Object on its own
can be picked up from anywhere and does nothing clever about it, which is what most props want.
Add one of these and the hand lands here instead; author a pose on it and the hand arrives in
that shape. Nothing about grips appears on the object until somebody asks for it.

A component on a child of the object rather than an entry in a list on it, because a grip point
is a position and an orientation before it is anything else. Put it where the hand should sit
and drag it in the scene view; a list of transform references has to be kept pointing at the
right objects by hand, and goes wrong silently when someone renames or reparents one.

The pose belongs here rather than on the object because it belongs to the *place*. Kept
on the object and keyed to the hand, as it was first built, an object gets one shape for the
left hand and one for the right - so a rifle cannot hold its grip differently from its
foregrip, and a mug cannot hold its handle differently from its body.

```csharp

```

### poses {#poses}

The hand shapes authored here, at most one per side. Written by the pose editor, not by hand.

Two, because [`allowedHand`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/GripPoint#allowedhand) may be [`Either`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/HandFilter#either) and the two
hands are not the same shape. A point that only one hand may take carries only that one.

### Constraints {#constraints}

What limits how the object may move while this point is held. Empty for an ordinary point,
which is most of them.

Both what this point carries and what the object itself carries. Which way a thing may move
usually depends on where it is held - a cabinet taken by its drawer front and by its door
handle moves two different ways - and those constraints belong on the points. Some do not:
a valve turns about its axle however you hold its rim, and that one freedom belongs to the
object. Authored once on the object, every point on it works the same constraint.

```csharp

```

### Allowed(Pose) {#allowed-pose}

Where the object is allowed to be, given where the hold would like it.

Every constraint here adds the one freedom it describes, starting from the object at rest -
so turn-about-an-axis and slide-along-it compose into a power cell, and anything none of
them allows is simply not in the answer. A mechanism is what the object may do, which
makes everything else what it may not.

public Pose Allowed(Pose wanted)

### AttachFor(GrabHand) {#attachfor-grabhand}

Where a hand taking this point should end up, in world space.

The point itself, unless a pose was authored here for this hand. What was authored is the
wrist; where a hand's grip sits relative to its wrist is a property of that hand, so the
hand supplies it here and the same authored pose fits a rig it was never authored on.

### Compose(IReadOnlyList\<GripConstraint>, Pose) {#compose-gripconstraint-pose}

Where a given set of constraints allows the object to be, given where the hold would like it.

Takes a list rather than reading its own, because an object can be held by two hands on two
grip points and only one of them may be the one carrying a mechanism. A shotgun is held by
its grip and pumped by its foregrip: what limits the gun is the foregrip's rail, and the
hand that writes the gun's velocity is the one on the grip, which has no rail of its own.
Asking only the writer's own point meant the pump was never consulted at all.

```csharp
public static Pose Compose(IReadOnlyList<GripConstraint> constraints, Pose wanted)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constraints` | `IReadOnlyList<GripConstraint>` | The constraints to compose, in order. |
| `wanted` | [`Pose`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Pose.html) | Where the hold would put the object if nothing limited it. |

**Returns** [`Pose`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Pose.html) - The pose they allow between them, or `wanted`if none of them apply.
